name: Contacts Journal CRM
description: Contacts Journal CRM is a personal relationship manager for Apple devices that keeps contacts, interaction logs, follow-up tasks, files, tags, groups, custom fields, and map context together. It helps independent professionals and small teams remember conversations, organize relationships, and plan timely outreach.
agentUseSummary: Contacts Journal CRM cannot yet be connected to Relay agents because its database and supported Siri Shortcuts execute through installed Apple-platform apps, while synchronization uses the user's own iCloud or Dropbox authority and Relay Marketplace does not currently ship that separate device-local connection model.

blocked.label: Connect Contacts Journal
blocked.description: Relay does not present a Contacts Journal purchase, Apple account, iCloud or Dropbox account, Apple Contacts permission, local database, or installed-app state as a Railway API connection.

blocked.label: Use Contacts Journal automation
blocked.description: Contacts Journal's official Siri Shortcuts require the installed app and local Apple Shortcuts execution that Relay cannot currently mount or trigger.

blocked.label: Access private CRM data
blocked.description: Relay does not inspect the local Contacts Journal database, Apple Contacts, private contacts, logs, tasks, files, fields, backups, app state, or private iCloud and Dropbox synchronization data.

blocked.label: Change CRM records
blocked.description: Creating, editing, tagging, grouping, merging, importing, exporting, completing, sharing, emailing, messaging, or deleting contacts and their CRM data remains unavailable until Relay ships explicit local execution and approval boundaries.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled until Relay ships a separately disclosed, user-authorized Apple-device connector using Contacts Journal's supported Shortcuts and explicit local permissions.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay does not silently bridge OpenClaw to Contacts Journal's local Siri Shortcuts, app database, Apple Contacts access, or private sync storage.
Relay does not silently bridge Hermes to Contacts Journal's local Siri Shortcuts, app database, Apple Contacts access, or private sync storage.

providerSetup.blocker: Contacts Journal stores contacts, logs, ToDos, files, and custom fields in an on-device database by default, requires user-granted Apple Contacts access for imported public contacts, and optionally syncs through the user's own iCloud or Dropbox account without giving the developer access to the data. Its official automation surface is a set of Siri and Apple Shortcuts actions that run through the installed app. The reviewed first-party materials do not document a server API, OAuth contract, webhook contract, or remote MCP service, and Relay's current Marketplace runtime excludes local-app command execution.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request Apple, iCloud, Dropbox, purchase, PIN, backup, or Contacts credentials; inspect local databases or files; run Shortcuts; automate the app UI; or show Connect. Reconsider after Relay ships a separately disclosed Apple-device connector with app presence, explicit Contacts and Shortcuts authorization, pinned reviewed actions, per-action approval, output redaction, audit, and no Railway or storage-account fallback.

evidence.supports: Contacts Journal describes its Apple-device personal CRM for contacts, logs, follow-ups, tags, custom fields, communication history, and iCloud synchronization.

Contacts Journal documents installed-app Shortcuts for finding contacts, logs, ToDos, and birthdays and for creating contacts, logs, ToDos, and tags, assigning tags, completing ToDos, and opening records.

Contacts Journal states that no account signup is required, its database lives on-device by default, the developer cannot access CRM data, and optional synchronization uses the user's own iCloud or Dropbox account.
Contacts Journal documents CloudSync as an installed-app setting that uses the same device iCloud account, with Dropbox available as a separate manual sync option.
Contacts Journal documents Apple system permission for full or selected contact access and states that contacts outside the user's grant remain unavailable to the app.

Contacts Journal requires external Google or Exchange contacts to be configured first in Apple Contacts, preserving those services as distinct underlying authorities rather than Contacts Journal credentials.
